units.function: Express route tests for returning the authenticated board user's persisted profile and updating display name/avatar for session or local-implicit identities.
units.dependencyDirection: Actor middleware supplies the trusted user id; auth routes read or update the users table and return a Paperclip-shaped synthetic session projection plus persisted user profile through the shared error handler.
units.keyDataModels: Board actor userId/source, user id/name/email/image, synthetic session id/userId, external HTTPS avatar URL, product asset-content path, null/omitted image update and validation error.
units.lifecycle: A signed-in board actor reads its current database profile. A profile PATCH updates name and optionally clears or replaces image; omitted image preserves the old value. HTTPS URLs and Paperclip asset-content paths are accepted, while a non-URL string is rejected.
units.testAssessment: Five route cases cover persisted session projection, local/session profile mutation, partial update semantics, internal asset paths and one invalid avatar. Database behavior is stubbed. Missing are unauthenticated/Agent access, row-not-found or cross-user updates, concurrent/versioned edits, name/image length and Unicode controls, non-HTTPS/data/file/javascript URLs, external-image privacy policy, internal asset ownership/tenant access, stable error code and audit event.
units.designRationale: Give the board UI a provider-independent current-user projection and editable human profile while supporting both externally hosted and product-managed avatar images.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a stable IdentityPort projection for real employees whose display profile is separate from authentication identity, organization authority and accountable-human certification.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the provider-neutral profile projection and partial-update semantics. Use opaque session subject rather than exposing a fabricated session identifier as authority; validate managed asset ownership, proxy or explicitly opt in external images to avoid tracking, add optimistic version and immutable profile-change audit, and keep IdP-bound legal identity fields non-editable through this endpoint.
units.responsibilityConflict: Display name and avatar can change without an audit receipt and are not distinguished from verified legal/employee identity. If responsibility records render only mutable profile fields, historical approver identity can be visually rewritten; evidence must pin opaque principal id plus identity snapshot/version.

units.function: Pure configuration tests for Better Auth cookie namespace isolation, secure-cookie selection, authentication rate limiting and trusted-origin derivation across deployment modes, exposure profiles, URLs, hostnames and resolved ports.
units.dependencyDirection: Deployment/bootstrap configuration and environment variables enter helper functions that build Better Auth advanced, rate-limit and trusted-origin options; the external Better Auth library derives concrete cookie names and enforces the resulting settings.
units.keyDataModels: Instance id and cookie prefix, deployment mode/exposure, auth base-URL mode, explicit/resolved public URL, secure-cookie boolean, rate-limit override, allowed hostname, configured/listen port and HTTP/HTTPS trusted origin.
units.lifecycle: Startup scopes cookies per instance, disables Secure for local HTTP/private auto-origin cases, retains it for HTTPS/public cases, enables auth rate limiting by default but accepts an explicit off override, and expands allowed hostnames into HTTP/HTTPS origin variants including the resolved non-default port.
units.testAssessment: Seventeen focused cases cover cookie naming, local/public/private URL combinations, default and overridden rate limiting, case-normalized hostnames and port resolution. Missing are SameSite/HttpOnly/domain/path/max-age, prefix sanitization/collision and cookie tossing, malformed/credentialed/IDNA/IPv6 origins, wildcard or proxy headers, CSRF flows, session rotation/revocation, distributed rate-limit storage/keying/bypass and a guard prohibiting rate-limit disablement on public profiles.
units.designRationale: Allow multiple local/worktree instances and mixed HTTP/HTTPS deployments without cookie collisions or broken sign-in, while supplying safe-ish auth defaults and host-derived origin trust.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs replaceable OIDC/SSO/local Identity adapters whose browser session policy is explicit per managed-cloud and self-hosted profile and cannot silently weaken due to URL autodetection.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the instance namespace, canonical-origin and resolved-listen-port test matrix at the Web adapter boundary. Enforce profile invariants: public production requires HTTPS Secure cookies and non-disableable distributed rate limiting; trusted origins must use explicitly configured schemes rather than automatically trusting both HTTP and HTTPS for every hostname. Keep Better Auth optional behind IdentityPort.
units.responsibilityConflict: Cookie/session configuration authenticates a browser but does not prove Company role or accountable authority. Explicitly disabling rate limiting is allowed even for public exposure, and auto-derived origins trust both schemes; operator configuration can therefore weaken identity assurance without a governed change record.
